Subject: Deployment mode follow-up — shared vs dedicated isolation & SLOs

Hi Sarah,

Thanks again for your time this afternoon — really appreciated the level of detail on your latency and compliance constraints. Quick recap from our call and recommended next steps: 

- Summary of options we discussed:
  * Hosted API (Redwood public): fastest to integrate, predictable performance for typical workloads, but no dedicated hardware guarantees — subject to multi-tenant scheduling and soft isolation measures.
  * Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools with tenancy isolation, SLA-backed uptime and throughput commitments, configurable autoscaling and burst policies.
  * Private (VPC / on-prem): full network/isolation control for regulated workloads, integration with customer KMS and audit pipelines.

- Your primary concerns: noisy-neighbor effects impacting tail latency, hard isolation boundaries for PII workloads, and measurable SLOs for token latency and throughput.

What I think makes sense based on our discussion: run an initial integration against Dedicated capacity (gives you the isolation + SLA you asked about) and then evaluate Private if you need customer-managed networking/KMS. Dedicated gives predictable p95/p99 tail characteristics and we can scope a short pilot to validate your worst-case load.

Next steps:
1) I'll loop in our solutions engineer (Marissa) and SE (Vivek) to share specific isolation/latency numbers and an architecture doc.
2) We'll provide a short Dedicated trial configuration plus the SLA summary and SOC2 attestation (attached).
3) If acceptable, FinTech procurement can review the commitment options and we’ll propose a Mutual Action Plan.

Attachments: Redwood_Dedicated_SLA_Summary.pdf, SOC2_Attestation_2026.pdf

If you want any numbers up front: can you share a representative 1-minute QPS and average request size (tokens)? I can use that to size the pilot nodes.

Thanks,

Hi Priyom / Sarah / Vivek,

Thanks — summarized answers and a recommended pilot below. Attaching the Dedicated architecture diagram and SLA summary for your review.

1) Observed latency (generation, comparable model family) — measured on Dedicated pools:
  - Typical p50: 25–40 ms per token
  - Typical p95: 90–160 ms per token (depends on sequence length & batch tuning)
  - Typical p99: 180–350 ms per token
Notes: these are measured under isolated Dedicated pools with continuous batching and KV cache warmed. Tail can increase if model context grows beyond planned sequence lengths; we'll size pilot nodes accordingly.

2) Isolation mechanisms in Dedicated:
  - Physical/resource isolation: Dedicated pools allocate entire GPU instances (no colocated tenants on the same GPU). We use per-tenant VM isolation + driver-level assignment to avoid cross-tenant GPU contention.
  - Kernel/resource controls: cgroups and scheduler priority for inference processes; I/O quotas for network-attached storage where applicable.
  - KV cache & memory: KV cache is sharded per-tenant; cache pressure is monitored and we reserve cache quotas for Dedicated tenants to prevent eviction from noisy workloads.
  - Networking: network egress/ingress shaping and VPC peering options for Private deployments.

3) Noisy-neighbor detection & remediation:
  - Detection: we run continuous telemetry (per-tenant GPU utilization, kernel queueing, cache miss rate, tail-latency heatmaps). Anomalies trigger automated alerts at p95/p99 deviations.
  - Immediate remediation options: live-scaled burst to reserved nodes in the same region, priority routing to warm nodes, and temporary throttling of non-critical background jobs.
  - Escalation: SE on-call page + a 24-hour SLA-backed incident response for Dedicated customers with enterprise contracts. We can include a clause for priority incident escalation in the agreement.

4) SLOs / SLA commitments we can propose for the pilot:
  - Availability: 99.9% monthly uptime for Dedicated capacity (SLA credit tiers in the doc).
  - Performance: we commit to providing baseline throughput capacity sized to your steady-state 60 rps with headroom for short bursts. We can define operational targets for p95 latency based on the pilot measurements.

Recommended pilot (2–4 weeks):
  - Dedicated pool sized for 60 rps steady state, with capacity to absorb short spikes to 120 rps for 30–60s (we recommend 20% headroom + 2 burst nodes).
  - Initial model and quantization profile to match your payload (~450 tokens).
  - Telemetry dashboard access + weekly check-ins to tune batching and sequence-length profiles.
  - Deliverables: runbook, architecture diagram, SLA summary, and a short scoring report at pilot end with p50/p95/p99 measurements under your workload.

Next steps: if that sounds good, I’ll share a formal Mutual Action Plan and a pilot order form. Priyom — want me to include any extra legal/procurement language for procurement?
